mongoDiag.allow.body: The tunnel will be allowed to open connections to {count, plural, one {this destination} other {these destinations}}. The list is part of the signed connection settings.
mongoDiag.allow.invalid.format: Not a valid host and port
mongoDiag.allow.invalid.linkLocal: Link-local and metadata addresses are never allowed
mongoDiag.allow.title: {count, plural, one {Allow this host?} other {Allow these # hosts?}}
mongoDiag.auth.failed.cause: The user name, password or authentication database is not right.
mongoDiag.auth.failed.fix1: Retype the user name and the password.
mongoDiag.auth.failed.fix3: Check that the user exists on this server.
mongoDiag.auth.failed.title: Sign-in failed
mongoDiag.auth.mechanism.cause: The server does not offer this mechanism, or this version does not support it.
mongoDiag.auth.mechanism.fix1: Choose Default, or the mechanism the user was created with.
mongoDiag.auth.mechanism.title: The sign-in method is not accepted
mongoDiag.auth.source.cause: The user lives in a different authentication database.
mongoDiag.auth.source.fix1: Set the authentication database to the one the user was created in (often admin).
mongoDiag.auth.source.title: The user is in another database
mongoDiag.auth.x509Subject.cause: The subject of the certificate is not a user in $external.
mongoDiag.auth.x509Subject.fix1: Create the user in $external with the subject of the certificate.
mongoDiag.auth.x509Subject.title: The certificate is not a known user
mongoDiag.authz.collection.cause: The user is signed in but has no right to read this namespace.
mongoDiag.authz.collection.fix1: Ask for the read role on this database or collection.
mongoDiag.authz.collection.title: Not allowed on this collection
mongoDiag.authz.command.cause: The user is signed in but has no right to run this command.
mongoDiag.authz.command.fix1: Ask for the read role on this database.
mongoDiag.authz.command.title: Not allowed to run this command
mongoDiag.authz.listDatabases.cause: Signed in, but this user may not list databases. The connection itself works.
mongoDiag.authz.listDatabases.fix1: Open a collection by typing its database name.
mongoDiag.authz.listDatabases.fix2: Ask for the listDatabases privilege on your own databases.
mongoDiag.authz.listDatabases.title: Databases cannot be listed
mongoDiag.config.fileMissing.cause: The CA, certificate or key file does not exist on this computer.
mongoDiag.config.fileMissing.fix2: File paths do not travel between computers, so a profile from another machine needs its files picked again.
mongoDiag.config.fileMissing.title: A file was not found
mongoDiag.config.invalid.cause: A field failed validation before anything was sent.
mongoDiag.config.invalid.fix1: Open the field marked in red and correct it.
mongoDiag.config.invalid.title: A setting is not valid
mongoDiag.config.needsSecret.cause: The password for this connection is not saved.
mongoDiag.config.needsSecret.fix1: Enter the password when asked, or save it in the Keychain.
mongoDiag.config.needsSecret.title: A password is needed
mongoDiag.config.pemInvalid.cause: The file could not be read as PEM. PKCS#12 (.p12, .pfx) is not supported.
mongoDiag.config.pemInvalid.fix2: Put the client certificate and its key in one file.
mongoDiag.config.pemInvalid.title: The file is not PEM
mongoDiag.config.plainRemote.cause: A password or PLAIN sign-in would travel without TLS to a host that is not on this computer.
mongoDiag.config.plainRemote.fix2: Or use SCRAM and do not save the password.
mongoDiag.config.plainRemote.title: Plain text to a remote host
mongoDiag.config.tlsRelaxRefused.cause: Production-level connections cannot skip certificate checks.
mongoDiag.config.tlsRelaxRefused.fix2: Or connect with the name the certificate was issued for.
mongoDiag.config.tlsRelaxRefused.title: Skipping certificate checks is not allowed
mongoDiag.config.unsupportedOption.cause: This version cannot honour the option (for example AWS, Kerberos or OIDC sign-in).
mongoDiag.config.unsupportedOption.fix1: Use SCRAM or X.509, or remove the option.
mongoDiag.config.unsupportedOption.title: An option is not supported
mongoDiag.dns.notFound.cause: The name does not resolve to an address.
mongoDiag.dns.notFound.fix1: Check the spelling of the host name.
mongoDiag.dns.notFound.fix2: Check your VPN and DNS. Split DNS can hide private names.
mongoDiag.dns.notFound.title: The host name was not found
mongoDiag.dns.srv.cause: The SRV record of the cluster name could not be looked up (private zone, no internet, or a wrong name).
mongoDiag.dns.srv.fix2: Or use a host list instead of an SRV address.
mongoDiag.dns.srv.title: The SRV lookup failed
mongoDiag.dns.txt.cause: The TXT record of the cluster name could not be looked up (private zone, no internet, or a wrong name).
mongoDiag.dns.txt.fix2: Or use a host list instead of an SRV address.
mongoDiag.dns.txt.title: The TXT lookup failed
mongoDiag.hint.atlas.authSource: Atlas: the authentication database is usually admin.
mongoDiag.hint.atlas.clusterName: Atlas: copy the cluster address from the Connect dialog.
mongoDiag.hint.atlas.databaseUser: Atlas: sign in with a Database User, not with your Atlas account.
mongoDiag.hint.atlas.networkAccess: Atlas: add the IP address of this computer under Network Access.
mongoDiag.hint.atlas.paused: Atlas: check that the cluster is not paused.
mongoDiag.hostkey.changed.body: This key differs from the one saved earlier. Connecting is blocked, and this dialog cannot override that.
mongoDiag.hostkey.compare: Compare this with the fingerprint your administrator gave you.
mongoDiag.hostkey.forget.done: The saved key was removed. Check the new fingerprint, then decide whether to trust it.
mongoDiag.hostkey.forget.failed: The saved key could not be removed.
mongoDiag.hostkey.forget.help: Use this only if the server was re-keyed on purpose. Only the key saved by this app is removed; your own known_hosts file is never edited.
mongoDiag.hostkey.forget.label: Type {host} to confirm
mongoDiag.hostkey.forget.title: Forget the saved key
mongoDiag.hostkey.scope: Only the SSH server itself is verified here. A hop configured with ProxyJump in your ssh config is not.
mongoDiag.hostkey.title.changed: The SSH host key has changed
mongoDiag.hostkey.title.unscannable: The host key cannot be scanned
mongoDiag.hostkey.trust.failed: The key could not be trusted. Scan again and compare the fingerprint.
mongoDiag.hostkey.unscannable.body: This SSH server is reached through ProxyJump, ProxyCommand or an alias, so it cannot be scanned directly.
mongoDiag.hostkey.unscannable.step1: Run this once in a terminal and accept the key there:
mongoDiag.members.allow: {count, plural, one {Allow this host} other {Allow these # hosts}}
mongoDiag.members.text: The server announced {count, plural, one {# member} other {# members}} that the tunnel does not allow yet.
mongoDiag.net.refused.cause: Nothing is listening on that host and port.
mongoDiag.net.refused.fix2: Check that the server is running and listens on an address this computer can reach.
mongoDiag.net.refused.title: Connection refused
mongoDiag.net.reset.cause: The server or a device on the way closed the connection.
mongoDiag.net.reset.fix2: Check firewall or proxy rules. Some servers also close connections that do not use TLS.
mongoDiag.net.reset.title: The connection was reset
mongoDiag.net.timeout.cause: The server did not answer in time. A firewall may be dropping the traffic.
mongoDiag.net.timeout.fix1: Check the host and the port.
mongoDiag.net.timeout.title: No answer in time
mongoDiag.net.unreachable.cause: There is no route from this computer to that network.
mongoDiag.net.unreachable.fix1: Check your internet connection or VPN.
mongoDiag.net.unreachable.fix2: Check the route to that network.
mongoDiag.net.unreachable.title: The network is unreachable
mongoDiag.other.cause: The error did not match a known case. The technical details hold the raw text.
mongoDiag.other.title: Could not connect
mongoDiag.result.title: Connection works
mongoDiag.select.direct.cause: Connecting directly to one server does not fit this deployment.
mongoDiag.select.direct.fix1: Toggle Connect directly to one server.
mongoDiag.select.direct.title: Direct and discovery mode do not match
mongoDiag.select.memberUnreachable.cause: The servers announce host names that this computer cannot reach.
mongoDiag.select.memberUnreachable.fix2: Or make the announced names resolvable from here.
mongoDiag.select.memberUnreachable.title: Members advertise unreachable names
mongoDiag.select.noServer.cause: The address answers in principle, but no server could be selected in time.
mongoDiag.select.noServer.fix1: Check the IP access list and the firewall.
mongoDiag.select.noServer.fix2: Check the replica set name and the Connect directly setting.
mongoDiag.select.noServer.fix3: Check that the cluster is running and not paused.
mongoDiag.select.noServer.title: No suitable server found
mongoDiag.select.replicaSetName.cause: The server belongs to a replica set with another name.
mongoDiag.select.replicaSetName.fix1: Use the name that rs.status() shows.
mongoDiag.select.replicaSetName.title: The replica set name differs
mongoDiag.stepper.label: Connection test steps
mongoDiag.timeout.total.cause: The whole attempt exceeded its time budget.
mongoDiag.timeout.total.title: The test took too long
mongoDiag.tls.clientCertRequired.cause: The server asked for a certificate that this connection did not send.
mongoDiag.tls.clientCertRequired.fix1: Add the client certificate file (PEM with certificate and key).
mongoDiag.tls.clientCertRequired.fix2: Add its passphrase if the key is encrypted.
mongoDiag.tls.clientCertRequired.title: A client certificate is required
mongoDiag.tls.expired.cause: The certificate is outside its validity period, or the clock of this computer is wrong.
mongoDiag.tls.expired.fix2: Check the date and time of this computer.
mongoDiag.tls.expired.title: The certificate is expired or not yet valid
mongoDiag.tls.hostname.cause: The certificate is not valid for the host name used to connect.
mongoDiag.tls.hostname.fix1: Connect with the name written on the certificate.
mongoDiag.tls.hostname.fix2: Add the CA file if you use a private CA.
mongoDiag.tls.hostname.fix3: Or connect through the tunnel, which keeps the real host names.
mongoDiag.tls.hostname.fix4: As a last resort, skip all certificate checks. This is never allowed at Production level.
mongoDiag.tls.hostname.title: The certificate is for another name
mongoDiag.tls.pem.cause: A certificate or key file could not be parsed.
mongoDiag.tls.pem.fix1: Make sure the file is PEM text with BEGIN and END lines.
mongoDiag.tls.pem.title: The PEM file cannot be read
mongoDiag.tls.serverNotTls.cause: TLS was requested but the server answered in plain text.
mongoDiag.tls.serverNotTls.fix1: Set TLS to Off for this server.
mongoDiag.tls.serverNotTls.fix2: Or enable TLS on the server.
mongoDiag.tls.serverNotTls.title: The server does not speak TLS
mongoDiag.tls.serverRequiresTls.cause: The server closes connections that do not use TLS.
mongoDiag.tls.serverRequiresTls.title: The server requires TLS
mongoDiag.tls.unknownIssuer.cause: The server certificate was not signed by a CA this app trusts. Only the built-in roots are used, not the system store.
mongoDiag.tls.unknownIssuer.fix2: Company or private CAs always need their CA file.
mongoDiag.tls.unknownIssuer.title: The certificate is not trusted
mongoDiag.tunnel.auth.cause: The user, key, agent identity or password was not accepted.
mongoDiag.tunnel.auth.fix2: For a key, check the file; for the agent, run ssh-add.
mongoDiag.tunnel.auth.title: The SSH server rejected the sign-in
mongoDiag.tunnel.dns.cause: The name of the SSH server does not resolve to an address.
mongoDiag.tunnel.dns.fix1: Check the spelling of the host.
mongoDiag.tunnel.dns.fix2: Check your VPN and DNS settings.
mongoDiag.tunnel.dns.title: The SSH server name was not found
mongoDiag.tunnel.dropped.cause: The SSH connection was closed or lost, for example after sleep or a network change.
mongoDiag.tunnel.dropped.title: The SSH tunnel ended
mongoDiag.tunnel.forwardingDisabled.caus: The SSH server does not allow this user to forward connections.
mongoDiag.tunnel.forwardingDisabled.fix1: Ask for AllowTcpForwarding yes for this user.
mongoDiag.tunnel.hostKeyChanged.cause: The server presents a different key than the saved one. That can mean a re-keyed server, or someone in the middle.
mongoDiag.tunnel.hostKeyChanged.fix1: Do not continue until you know why.
mongoDiag.tunnel.hostKeyChanged.fix2: Ask the administrator whether the server was re-keyed.
mongoDiag.tunnel.hostKeyChanged.fix3: If it was, forget the saved key (you type the host name), then trust a fresh scan.
mongoDiag.tunnel.hostKeyChanged.title: The SSH host key changed
mongoDiag.tunnel.hostKeyUnknown.cause: This computer has not seen the host key of the server before.
mongoDiag.tunnel.hostKeyUnknown.fix1: Compare the fingerprint with the one your administrator gave you.
mongoDiag.tunnel.hostKeyUnknown.fix2: If it matches, trust it and connect.
mongoDiag.tunnel.hostKeyUnknown.title: First contact with this SSH server
mongoDiag.tunnel.hostKeyUnscannable.caus: The SSH server is reached through ProxyJump, ProxyCommand or an alias, so it cannot be scanned directly.
mongoDiag.tunnel.hostKeyUnscannable.fix1: Run ssh with the host name once in a terminal and accept the key there.
mongoDiag.tunnel.hostKeyUnscannable.titl: The host key cannot be checked here
mongoDiag.tunnel.interactive.cause: The SSH server wants a second factor or another prompt that this app cannot answer.
mongoDiag.tunnel.interactive.fix1: Use a key or the SSH agent instead.
mongoDiag.tunnel.interactive.fix2: Or start your own ssh -D tunnel and use the SOCKS5 option.
mongoDiag.tunnel.interactive.title: The server asks for more than a password
mongoDiag.tunnel.ipv6.cause: The tunnel cannot forward to an IPv6 address.
mongoDiag.tunnel.ipv6.title: IPv6 addresses are not supported
mongoDiag.tunnel.keyFile.cause: The key file is missing or is not a private key.
mongoDiag.tunnel.keyFile.fix1: Pick the private key file again.
mongoDiag.tunnel.keyFile.fix2: Use the private key, not the .pub file.
mongoDiag.tunnel.keyFile.title: The key file cannot be used
mongoDiag.tunnel.keyPerms.cause: ssh refuses a private key that other users can read.
mongoDiag.tunnel.keyPerms.fix1: Run chmod 600 on the key file.
mongoDiag.tunnel.keyPerms.title: The key file is too open
mongoDiag.tunnel.network.cause: The connection to the SSH host or port failed or timed out.
mongoDiag.tunnel.network.fix1: Check the host and the port.
mongoDiag.tunnel.network.title: The SSH server is not reachable
mongoDiag.tunnel.noSsh.cause: /usr/bin/ssh is missing, is not owned by root, or is too old for password and passphrase sign-in (OpenSSH 8.4 or newer is needed).
mongoDiag.tunnel.noSsh.fix2: Sign-in with the SSH agent or an unencrypted key still works with an older version.
mongoDiag.tunnel.noSsh.title: No usable ssh program
mongoDiag.tunnel.notAllowed.cause: The tunnel only forwards to the hosts you listed, and {host} is not one of them.
mongoDiag.tunnel.notAllowed.fix1: Allow this host. The button names the exact host and port.
mongoDiag.tunnel.notAllowed.fix2: Or use Discover members after a successful test and allow them all.
mongoDiag.tunnel.notAllowed.title: This database host is not allowed
mongoDiag.tunnel.passphrase.cause: The key is encrypted and the passphrase did not unlock it.
mongoDiag.tunnel.passphrase.title: The key passphrase is wrong
mongoDiag.tunnel.targetRefused.cause: The SSH server refused or could not open the connection to the database host.
mongoDiag.tunnel.targetRefused.fix1: Use the database host name as the SSH server sees it.
mongoDiag.tunnel.targetRefused.fix2: Check that the database is running and its port is open towards the SSH server.
mongoDiag.tunnel.targetRefused.title: The SSH server cannot reach the database
mongoDiag.view.likely: Based on the error text, so treat this as a likely cause.
mongoDiag.warning.plainRemote: The connection is not encrypted and the server is not on this computer.
mongoDiag.warning.relaxed: Certificate checks are skipped for this connection.
mongoDiag.warning.writer: This account can write. The app still only reads, but the account is more powerful than needed.
